title: Bug Hunt 4: The Shared Default
prompt: Every call to add_task seems to remember previous calls — tasks pile up across calls. Fix WITHOUT removing the default: make each call start from a fresh list (or make the parameter required).
boilerplate:
def add_task(task, tasks=[]):
    tasks.append(task)
    return tasks

add_task("a")
add_task("b")
result = add_task("c")
print(result)

tests.name: each call is fresh
tests.code:
assert len(printed) == 1 and "c" in printed[0] and "a" not in printed[0] and "b" not in printed[0], f"got {printed}"
assert "[]" not in code.split("def add_task")[1].split(")")[0], "no mutable default allowed"
tests.hint: The mutable default is created ONCE at definition time and shared. Fix: tasks=None, then tasks = [] inside the function.
